newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS - German roasters raising retail coffee prices.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - German roasters raising retail coffee prices.

text.p: German coffee roasters are once again battling to enforce higher retail prices, but analysts said the market is competitive and often resistant to such attempts.
Market leader Kraft Jacobs Suchard (KJS), part of Philip Morris Cos Inc, said on Friday it would probably announce price hikes ex-plant for roasted coffee within the next week.
The number two, Tchibo Frisch-Roest Kaffee GmbH, added up to one mark to each 500-gram packet of the high-quality coffee on sale in its 20,000 shops.
"The problem is that earlier price increases have not fully reached the consumer," a coffee analyst said.
"Wholesalers have hoarded coffee and supermarkets are taking deliberate losses in coffee to lure consumers into their shops."
Roasters operating through the wholesale trade said in March they would raise their ex-works prices by 2.50 marks.
But average prices on German supermarket shelves had only risen to 7.23 marks by April 20 from 6.78 marks at the beginning of 1997.
"The price rises still have to wind their way through the system, that's why roasters are so nervous," the analyst said.
In addition, a seasonal drop in consumption is expected in the spring and summer months, while many households have been hoarding coffee after the initial round of price increases.
Roasters in Germany, the world's second largest market with an annual consumption of 564,000 tonnes of green coffee, are grappling with the effects of fresh global price rallies.
Concerns about Latin American supply and low consumer stocks have brought price increases of 16 percent on the New York futures market this week.

In mark terms, price volatility affects roasters in Germany worse than elsewhere. Green coffee prices have risen by 80 percent since December while the dollar has climbed to 1.72 from 1.50 marks and shows no signs of easing.

Tchibo and Eduscho GmbH & Co KG, which Tchibo bought last December, together accounted for 25-26 percent of the market in the first quarter of 1997 and can enact price increases directly and immediately.
Tchibo's average price is now just under 10 marks per 500 grams and Eduscho's is in a 6.99-9.99 marks range.
But the latest price rise by KJS might be spoilt by what market sources call "the Aldi factor" and competitors' reluctance to follow suit.
The analyst said retail discounter Aldi was offering coffee at an average 5.60 marks.
Melitta Kaffee GmbH said it believed prices should rise but the market might resist attempts to raise them. "There are no talks underway on this subject," a spokeswoman said.
Melitta is only the fourth largest roaster but its aggressive pricing policy can tilt the market one way or another.
An official at Darboven, a family-owned firm controlling a 12 percent market share, said the necessity for price rises had been acknowledged but no decision had yet been taken.
Sources at roaster Alois Dallmayr Kaffee oHG in Munich were not available for comment on Friday. --Hamburg newsroom, +49-40-41903275
